questions.title: Sequential Promise Resolution
questions.description:
Implement a function `sequentialResolution` that takes in an array of **promises**, `promises`, and an array of **indices**, `order`. The promises should be resolved in the order of the indices in the `order` array. After each promise is resolved, push the returned value from the promise to a global array `resolvedPromises`.

If a promise fails to resolve, the function should throw an error, and no further promises should be resolved. The error message should be **"Error Thrown"** (without quotes). The function should not return anything.

Each promise `i` uses a variable, `promises[i]` provided in the input. It resolves and returns `promises[i]` if it is not equal to 0. If it is equal to 0, the function rejects and returns an error message **"Error"** (without quotes).

For example, if `order = [2, 1, 3]`, `promises = [1, 2, 1]`, then the second promise should be resolved first, followed by the first and third promises. Here, no promise is rejected. Promises are resolved as `[2, 1, 1]`.

### Function Signature

```javascript
function sequentialResolution(promises, order) {
  // Your code here
}
```

### Parameters

- `promises[promises[0], ...promises[n-1]]`: an array of promises
- `order[order[0], ...order[n-1]]`: an array of 1-based indices

### Constraints

- `1 ≤ n, promises[i] ≤ 100`
- Array `order` is a permutation of integers 1 to n.
- It is guaranteed that either one or no promise is rejected.

### Sample Case 0

**Input:** `promises = [1, 2, 0, 1]`, `order = [2, 1, 3, 4]`

**Output:**
```
2
1
Error Thrown
```

**Explanation:** The second promise should be resolved first followed by the first. The third promise is rejected, and an error is thrown with the message "Error Thrown".

### Sample Case 1

**Input:** `promises = [3, 4, 1, 3]`, `order = [1, 4, 2, 3]`

**Output:**
```
3
3
4
1
```

**Explanation:** The first promise should be resolved first followed by the fourth, the second, and the third. No promise is rejected.

questions.title: Array.map() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `Array.prototype.myMap` that mirrors native `Array.map()`.

Here **this** points to the array itself — the object before the dot.

### Example

```javascript
console.log([1, 2, 3].myMap(x => x * 2));
// [2, 4, 6]
```

Complete the implementation in the editor.

testCases.setup: const arr = [1, , 3]; const result = arr.myMap(x => x * 2);
testCases.code: result.length === 3 && 0 in result && !(1 in result) && result[0] === 2 && result[2] === 6

questions.title: Array.filter() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `Array.prototype.myFilter` that mirrors native `Array.filter()`.

Return a new array with elements where the callback returns a truthy value. Skip sparse holes using `i in this`.

### Signature

```javascript
Array.prototype.myFilter = function (callback, thisArg) { }
```

Complete the implementation in the editor.

questions.title: Array.reduce() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `Array.prototype.myReduce` that mirrors native `Array.reduce()`.

### Example

```javascript
[1, 2, 3].myReduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
// 6
```

Support both with and without an `initialValue`. Complete the implementation in the editor.

questions.title: Function.call() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `Function.prototype.myCall` that invokes a function with a given `this` value and arguments.

### Signature

```javascript
Function.prototype.myCall = function (context, ...args) { }
```

Preserve `this` context. Default `context` to `globalThis` when nullish. Complete the implementation in the editor.

testCases.setup: function add(a, b) { return this.x + a + b; }

questions.title: Function.apply() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `Function.prototype.myApply` — like `myCall`, but arguments are passed as an array.

### Signature

```javascript
Function.prototype.myApply = function (context, args = []) { }
```

Complete the implementation in the editor.

testCases.setup: function add(a, b) { return this.x + a + b; }

questions.title: Flatten Array (infinite)
questions.description:
Implement `flatten(arr)` that flattens a nested array to any depth.

### Example

```javascript
flatten([1, [2, [3, [4]]]]);
// [1, 2, 3, 4]
```

Complete the implementation in the editor.

questions.title: Flatten with Level
questions.description:
Implement `flatten(arr, depth = 1)` that flattens only up to the given depth.

### Example

```javascript
flatten([1, [2, [3, [4]]]], 2);
// [1, 2, 3, [4]]
```

Complete the implementation in the editor.

questions.title: Debounce

testCases.setup: let count = 0; const fn = () => count++; const debounced = debounce(fn, 100);

questions.title: Throttle
questions.description:
Implement `throttle(fn, delay)` that invokes `fn` at most once per `delay` ms window.

Rapid calls within the window should be ignored. Complete the implementation in the editor.

testCases.setup: let count = 0; const fn = () => count++; const throttled = throttle(fn, 100);

questions.title: Promise Polyfill
questions.description:
Implement a basic `MyPromise` class with `then` and `catch`.

Support resolving, rejecting, and chaining. Handlers registered while `pending` should run once settled.

Complete the implementation in the editor.

testCases.code: await new MyPromise((_, reject) => reject("err")).catch(e => e)

questions.title: Promise.all() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `promiseAll(promises)` that resolves when all promises settle successfully.

Reject on the first failure. Return results in input order. Empty array resolves to `[]`.

Complete the implementation in the editor.

questions.title: Promise.race() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `promiseRace(promises)` that settles with the first promise to fulfill or reject.

Complete the implementation in the editor.

questions.title: Promise.any() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `promiseAny(promises)` that resolves with the first fulfilled promise.

If all reject, reject with `AggregateError`. Empty input rejects with `AggregateError([])`.

Complete the implementation in the editor.

testCases.code: await promiseAny([Promise.reject("a"), Promise.reject("b")]).catch(e => e instanceof AggregateError)

questions.title: Promise.allSettled() polyfill
questions.description:
Implement `promiseAllSettled(promises)` that waits for every promise and never rejects.

Return `{ status: "fulfilled", value }` or `{ status: "rejected", reason }` per index.

Complete the implementation in the editor.
